subject: Architecture
title: Rammed Earth: Ancient Walls, Modern Homes
description: A quick, practical guide to Rammed Earth: Ancient Walls, Modern Homes.

hook.text: Rammed earth walls are made by compacting soil into forms — the same technique used 10,000 years ago.

buildup.text: Layers of damp earth are pounded into wooden forms, creating dense walls with beautiful natural stripes.

discovery.text: Sections of the Great Wall of China are rammed earth — and have stood for over 2,000 years.

twist.text: Modern rammed earth uses a small amount of cement for added strength while keeping 90% natural soil.

climax.text: Rammed earth walls regulate humidity naturally, absorbing and releasing moisture as conditions change.

punchline.text: The oldest building technique is also one of the greenest.

quiz.question: What ancient structure uses rammed earth construction?
options: Sections of the Great Wall of China

details.summary: Rammed earth construction compacts damp soil into formwork to create solid walls with excellent thermal mass and minimal embodied carbon. Used for thousands of years — sections of the Great Wall of China are rammed earth — the technique is now experiencing a renaissance in sustainable modern.
details.whyItMatters: Rammed earth uses the most abundant building material on the planet — dirt — with minimal processing or energy input. Its thermal mass stores and releases heat naturally, reducing energy needs in climates with daily temperature swings.
takeaways: Damp soil compacted into formwork creates solid thermal mass walls
Used for millennia, including sections of the Great Wall of China
Minimal embodied carbon compared to concrete or brick construction

faq.question: How strong are rammed earth walls?
faq.answer: Stabilized rammed earth (with 5-10% cement) achieves compressive strengths of 4-20 MPa, comparable to low-grade concrete. Unstabilized rammed earth walls have lower strength but have supported multi-story buildings for centuries. In earthquake zones, reinforcement with steel or bamboo is added.

faq.question: Do rammed earth buildings last?
faq.answer: Exceptionally well in appropriate climates. Rammed earth sections of the Great Wall have survived over 2,000 years. The technique works best in arid or semi-arid climates. In wet climates, wide roof overhangs and damp-proof courses protect walls from erosion.
